slides.title: My final ICT task
lines: Use the skills from this half-term.
Make a clear update for a small group.
Keep your work and answers private.
slides.cue: Point, write, type or speak quietly to an adult.
slides.notes: Assessing week. Model on different data before the timed task. Do not require reading aloud, a live talk or public answers. Record support and evidence separately for each pupil.

slides.title: My files are ready
lines: Find your earlier ICT files with the adult.
Keep each original file. Work in new copies.
Use a task label, with no personal details.
slides.notes: Before arrival, make earlier outputs easy to find. Use ICT_Practice/W07_Final and A or B task labels. Record adult-prepared copies as preparation, not pupil file-management evidence. Missing earlier work is recorded, not recreated as though it were original.

slides.title: A source for this task
lines: Two notes give different points for card.
Which one is checked for this kit?
Give a reason using the source card.
slides.cue: Make your own choice before checking.
slides.notes: Use the two source cards from the pupil brief. Collect a private answer before any reveal. Date alone does not prove reliability: purpose, checked status and match to the task matter. This pre-task response can inform assessment, with support recorded.

slides.title: A separate worked example
lines: Watch the adult use different kit data.
Two strip packs use 3 points each.
The row total is 2 times 3, which is 6.
The formula uses the two input cells.
slides.cue: Point to the inputs in the model.
slides.notes: Use a disposable example with strip packs 2 at 3 points and tab packs 1 at 4. Model a cell-reference product, total 10, and chart of 6 and 4 without the total row. Do not complete the pupil task data. Fade to one place prompt, then independent work.

slides.title: A short explanation
lines: A useful paragraph explains the work.
Name the source and one check.
Say what the chart shows.
Explain a choice that helps the reader.
slides.cue: Use the frame if it helps you explain.
slides.notes: Model with the separate example: I used the checked brief for this kit. My product formula gives 6 points for strips. Strips use 2 more points than tabs. I added a chart description so its facts are available without the image. Do not leave this model as pupil-authored evidence.

slides.title: What counts as evidence?
lines: A saved file shows a result.
A seen action shows how you made it.
Record the help you used.
slides.cue: Keep earlier work and today's work distinct.
slides.notes: Explain evidence before work starts. Prior work retains its original date and support record. A finished file alone does not prove independence. Exact scribing is access support; supplied reasoning or corrections must be recorded separately.

slides.title: The checks before work
lines: Watch a copy save and reopen.
Check one chart value against its source.
On a slide, check the title comes first.
slides.cue: Point to one check you will use.
slides.notes: Use the separate model. Show where alternative text and reading order are set, without answering the assessed source or totals. Check title, chart, comparison using the software order tool. Check pupils can locate the brief, then use the private hinge on the next slide within this slot.

slides.title: A total in the chart
lines: A chart compares two kit items.
It also has a bar for the whole total.
Does that third bar represent another item?
slides.cue: Give a private answer with a reason.
slides.notes: Hinge before the timed task: no, whole total combines the items. Re-model within this slot if needed. Parallel hinge: a chart description says image.png. Does it convey the data? No. Record any prompt used. Do not cold call.
answers: No. Leave the whole total out of the item chart.
A file name does not explain the chart data.

slides.title: My kit update

Make formulas and a chart of the items.

slides.cue: Work privately. Choose a route and record support.
slides.notes: Slides 9-12 share 18 minutes. Suggested split: formulas and chart 7; document 5; slide and save 6. Use a copy of an earlier document/slide or a blank file if missing. Collect independent first responses before prompts. One device: two nine-minute turns with paper planning alongside; record incomplete digital actions for follow-up, never infer completion.

pupil_pages.title: Final task step cards
sections: Today I can
I can use my ICT skills to make and check a clear kit update.
1 Choose and protect
Read the two source cards. Choose the source for this kit and give a reason. Use only made-up kit facts. Keep personal details out of the files.
2 Work out and chart
Check the starter inputs. Use formulas for each row and the whole total. Make a chart of the three items, with clear labels and points. Leave the whole total out.
3 Explain in a document
Use a title, a heading and a short paragraph. Explain the source, a formula, the chart and one access choice. The frame is on the word page.
4 Update one slide
Use a copy of an earlier slide or a blank slide. Add the new chart, a useful title and a short comparison. Use clear text. Give the chart a useful description and check its reading order.
5 Save and gather
Save and reopen the task files. Use the evidence sheet to locate outputs from all seven weeks. Record any missing work and the help used.
Private responses
Plan in your book or type privately. Point or speak quietly to an adult. No reading aloud or live talk is needed.

plan_pages.title: Teacher and cover plan
sections: Lesson

My final ICT task | Tuesday 15 December 2026 | Tuesday P6 | 40 minutes
Year A. LAUNCH pair. Assessing week.
Aim
I can use my ICT skills to make and check a clear kit update.
Theme
Identity & Belonging: communicate a fictional kit plan so others can use it. No personal profile or access disclosure is required.
Careers
A short account of checked work can support an application. Use a saved example to explain a skill and the help you used.
Prepare

Use the fourteen-slide lesson or HTML and the Assessment_Start spreadsheet. Prepare each pupil earlier outputs from Weeks 1-6 for private access. Make document and slide copies available, keeping originals. Missing work is logged. Offer the task brief, one route and the evidence sheet in ordinary or pink print. Two devices are preferred.
Participation

Model first on different data. Use private answers, pointing, typing, books or quiet talk. No cold calling, required reading aloud or public presentation. The paragraph frame is available to all. Record access support separately from supplied reasoning.
Success

I used the right source and checked my results.
I made clear files for the reader.
I gathered evidence and recorded the help I used.

plan_pages.title: Lesson sequence
sections: 0 to 3 minutes  Arrival
Slides 1-2. Find earlier outputs, protect originals and choose task labels. Adult preparation is not pupil file-management evidence.
3 to 6  Starter
Slide 3. Private source choice from the two task cards. Capture the first response and support used.
6 to 10  Model calculation
Slide 4. Use strip packs 2 at 3 and tab packs 1 at 4. Model products 6 and 4, total 10 and chart range excluding total.
10 to 12  Model paragraph
Slides 5-6. Model a short explanation on the separate data. Explain how evidence and support will be recorded.
12 to 15  Guided checks
Slides 7-8. Model copy-save-reopen, image description and order. Private hinge: whole total is not another item. Re-model if needed within the slot.
15 to 33  Assessed task
Slides 9-12. Formulas and chart about 7 minutes; document 5; one updated slide and saving 6. Keep answer reveals closed until first attempts are recorded.
33 to 38  Evidence
Slide 13. Gather seven weeks of work through the index. Inspect current files and record observed actions, prior evidence and gaps separately.
38 to 40  Exit
Slide 14. One success, one next step, private response and acknowledgement. Keep unfinished checks pending.

plan_pages.title: Assessment and adaptations
sections: Before support

Observe and retain the first attempt before giving a reasoning prompt or correcting a result. Do not count copying a supplied answer as an independent skill. Routes are access choices, not attainment grades.
Record for each skill

Use on own, access support, reasoning prompt, or not yet seen, with the actual action, date and file or book location. Exact scribing can preserve pupil reasoning but does not prove independent typing. Adult-made files do not prove pupil editing.
Cognition and learning
Show one chunk at a time. Keep the brief and word page visible. Fade the separate model. Use the prompt ladder: point, short question, rephrase, scaffold or choice, model first step only.
Communication and EAL
Use the paragraph frame, quiet talk, pointing and planning in any language. Staff may read privately on request. Keep meaning and digital action evidence distinct.
SEMH and physical access
Offer predictable stages, a quiet pause within the task time, pink paper, zoom and uncluttered views. Avoid comparison between pupils. Record exact adult typing and any further prompts.
One device or missing files

Use two nine-minute device turns with book planning alongside. If this prevents completion, prioritise formula and chart evidence, then the document and slide. Record the remaining actions for a later check. A blank document or slide may replace a missing starter but is dated today, not backfilled as earlier work.

plan_pages.title: Evidence and follow up
sections: Seven week collection

The evidence sheet indexes all seven weeks. Record actual pupil file paths or book pages, original dates, found or missing status and support. Referencing an earlier output does not make it a new independent observation.
Assessed checks

Inspect safe file handling and source choice; document title and heading; row and total formulas; chart range and meaning; slide readability, image description and order; paragraph reasoning. The staff guide gives criteria and answers. Use qualitative evidence, not an invented accreditation grade.
Saving

Use ICT_Practice/W07_Final. Kit_A_v1 or Kit_B_v1 may be used for the document, spreadsheet and presentation because their extensions differ. Keep originals. Reopen each saved file. Aspire uses v2 and keeps v1.
Feedback

Give one specific success and one NS. Record VF, WS or I only as observed. Allow the pupil to respond in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode or private mode. Use R after the response and adult acknowledgement.
Limits and absence

Paper work can show source reasoning and planned calculations, not software edits. If an image-description or order control is unavailable, record that check not yet. Native playback and screen-reader checks need the intended application. Arrange a later check for missing or incomplete evidence.
End of sequence
Week 7 closes the approved ICT half-term. Retain the evidence index with the outputs. Creative Arts Spring 1 begins only after the next owner brief.

staff_pages.title: Staff answers and checks
sections: Source and privacy

Source A is checked for this kit and gives the required inputs. Source B is an unchecked older draft with a conflicting card rate. Date alone is insufficient. Use fictional kit facts and task labels, with no personal details.
Formulas and values

Task!D4 = B4*C4 gives 12. D5 = B5*C5 gives 10. D6 = B6*C6 gives 6. D7 = SUM(D4:D6) gives 28. Equivalent cell-reference formulas are valid. Inspect formulas rather than values alone. Typing 12, 10, 6 and 28 does not show formula use.
Chart

Plot Paper packs 12, Card packs 10 and Fastener packs 6. Exclude the whole total 28. Use a clear title, item labels and total points, with a zero baseline. Paper uses 2 more points than card and 6 more than fasteners. Points do not show price or popularity.
Paragraph and document

Accept a title, heading and coherent short paragraph. Example meaning: source A fits this checked kit; a product formula multiplies pack count by points each; paper needs most points; one stated access choice helps the reader. The pupil may use the frame but supplies the reasoning.
Slide

One current slide is enough. Accept a clear kit title, new chart and correct comparison. Use readable dark text, useful chart description and title-chart-comparison reading order verified in the software. A visible caption alone does not prove the alternative-text field was set.
Aspire

Paper packs changed from 3 to 4 gives paper 16, card 10, fasteners 6, whole total 32. Chart and narrative must match v2. Preserve v1. A static chart image and its description need updating separately.

staff_pages.title: Assessment evidence guide
sections: Files and sources
Record new copy, clear task label and reopen. Check personal details are absent. Record the source choice and a task-specific reason before feedback.
Document
Look for a useful title, heading, readable paragraph and correct facts. Record what the pupil changed today and what came from the earlier document.
Calculation and chart

Watch one formula entry or inspect it with the pupil explaining the references. Check the total formula includes each item once. Check chart categories, row values and a correct comparison. Record copying or supplied formulas.
Slide and explanation

Observe a readability choice, description setting and order check. Retain the paragraph explanation of the source, formula, comparison and access choice. A strong spoken reason alone does not prove software editing.
Evidence status

For each skill, record on own, access support, reasoning prompt or not yet seen, plus date, file or book location and exact help. Prior evidence has its original date. Missing evidence stays missing. No numerical pass threshold or external award is implied.
Review and feedback

Use one next step linked to a gap, such as checking a chart range or explaining a source. Retain the response and acknowledge it privately. A portfolio file count is not proof of the skills within it.
Hinges
Whole total is a sum of items, not another item for the comparison chart. An image file name does not describe the data. If either is unclear, re-model before the task and record the prompt.

staff_pages.title: Support adult brief
sections: Before
Prepare earlier files and fresh copies. Offer the brief, chosen route, word page and evidence sheet. Check one private response mode. Keep supplied lesson resources separate from pupil outputs.
Model
Use the separate strip and tab data. Demonstrate one action, then fade. Do not complete the task totals or source reason for the pupil.
During the task
Allow the first attempt. Use the prompt ladder when needed. Record the exact support at the time. Distinguish locating a control or exact scribing from giving a formula, reason or correction.
Time and turn taking
Two devices are preferred. With one device, each pupil has nine minutes while the other plans in their book. Record unfinished actions for a later check; do not rush or infer skills from paper plans.
Evidence
Locate all seven weeks of actual outputs. Record missing files, original dates and today's observations. Do not create replacement work and label it as historical evidence.
Close
Help pupils save and reopen. Give one next step, allow a private response and acknowledge it. No reading aloud or live presentation is needed.

sequence_pages.title: Sequence and evidence guide
sections: The approved sequence

Year A, Autumn 2. Week 1 files and personal information; Week 2 structured document; Week 3 evaluating sources; Week 4 spreadsheet formulas; Week 5 charts; Week 6 accessible presentation; Week 7 independent task with a paragraph frame, assessing.
This lesson
Tuesday 15 December 2026, P6. Week commencing 14 December. One 40-minute lesson for the LAUNCH pair. School and Public teaching content is identical and generic.
Final task

Use fictional new kit inputs to produce a formula spreadsheet and chart, a short structured document and one updated slide. The supplied starter holds inputs only; formulas, chart and explanations are pupil work.
Seven week evidence

The evidence sheet gathers actual output locations for Weeks 1-7. Keep original dates and support records. Separate prior evidence, today's observations and missing work. Do not infer independence from a polished file or a route label.
Access and follow up

Model first with different data. Offer pink print, private answers, exact scribing with support recorded, and no compulsory reading aloud or cold calling. Paper planning does not prove digital actions. Schedule any missing software checks later.
After this return
The ICT half-term is complete. Creative Arts Spring 1 Week 1, Explore pathway, BUILD and GROW, awaits the owner's brief after acceptance.
